description: Shared Renovate preset for the stefgo repositories. See README.md for why each setting is what it is.

packageRules.description: Action updates are CI changes, as they were with Dependabot.
chore by default: a fix commit cuts a patch release, and a build tool, a test or a linter changes nothing a user runs. What does reach the running system is made fix(deps) by the runtime rule below.

One pull request a week for every minor and patch update that stays out of the running system. Renovate merges one pull request per run, so with a daily run each separate one would cost a day. The Python and Node versions stay out: they are merged by hand and would hold the whole group. A group mixes ci and chore updates, so the type is set; neither cuts a release.

The running system: npm dependencies (not devDependencies) -- what an image keeps after npm prune --omit=dev and what a card bundles --, the base images of the shipped Dockerfiles (not *.dev) and the lock file refresh. fix(deps), so bump auto releases it as a patch, and noted in .release/next.md, because a release with nothing written there is refused. See scripts/release-note.mjs.
matchJsonata: (manager = 'npm' and depType = 'dependencies') or (manager = 'dockerfile' and $not($contains(packageFile, '.dev'))) or updateType = 'lockFileMaintenance'

packageRules.description: The minor and patch updates of the running system travel in a group of their own: it is a fix and writes the notes, the development group does neither. Same condition as the rule above; the Python and Node versions stay out for the same reason as there.
matchJsonata: (manager = 'npm' and depType = 'dependencies') or (manager = 'dockerfile' and $not($contains(packageFile, '.dev'))) or updateType = 'lockFileMaintenance'

packageRules.description: Python and Node versions follow what Home Assistant, the card toolchain and the engines field of a package support, not the newest release -- in the workflows, in .nvmrc and in a Dockerfile's base image alike. Proposed, but merged by hand.
A compromised npm release is usually found and pulled within hours. Waiting three days keeps it out; security updates do not wait.

Home Assistant sets the Python version the tests run on: pytest-homeassistant-custom-component follows the interpreter HA requires, and on an older one pip silently resolves a months-old Home Assistant instead of failing. Raise this bound once HA moves to the next Python.
Python test requirements are open ranges (>=) on purpose; an update inside the range needs no pull request.
